minutes.summary: The committee heard budget presentations from the public access cable committee, the sewer commission and the Board of Health (whose Nashoba assessment rose with population). The only vote was adjournment.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no votes except adjournment; it heard budget presentations and reviewed the draft warrant's money articles.
The sewer commission described a planned rate increase for FY23 and a budget that still runs a deficit, with debt service exceeding betterment revenue for a few years.
The committee walked through the draft warrant's moneyed articles, including a snow and ice budget amendment, and asked for a funding-source chart next week.
The public access cable committee presented a budget in which spending exceeds income, with the gap drawn from retained earnings.
The Board of Health presented its budget, including the Nashoba assessment, and the committee then set a warrant letter deadline and a tentative public hearing date.

why_it_matters: The sewer rate increase would show up on sewer bills for ratepayers, and the budget's deficit means the sewer fund is drawing on retained earnings.

The warrant articles the committee reviewed are the money questions town meeting voters will be asked to decide, so next week's bracketed estimates and funding-source chart are the first look at how they would be paid for.
watch_next: Next week's meeting: votes on the moneyed articles with bracketed estimates, the funding-source chart for the budget adjustment article, and the warrant letter.
The tentative April 14 public hearing, to be advertised next week to meet the April 1 posting deadline.

The main differences are the PAC income estimate ($197,857 in ours vs $200,285 officially), a sewer retained-earnings transfer only our minutes record, and a few follow-up decisions that appear in only one record.
